title: .dev-workflow/signals/status.json
description: The workspace agent's progress signal — written by the workspace, read by the main session and the autopilot tick. This is the ONLY input the orchestrator has from a workspace: the main session reads these fields and updates product-context.yaml, and a workspace never writes that file itself. A field the orchestrator needs but this document does not declare is a field the orchestrator cannot route on.

phase.description: Current phase. A workspace's own run ends at 12 (merge); Phase 13 (archive) runs from the main session via /aep-wrap.

blockers.description: What is preventing progress. Appended the moment a blocker appears, not at the next phase boundary — a declared blocker is what distinguishes a blocked workspace from a silent one in the stuck ladder.

story_status.description: Story state for /aep-dispatch sync. Set in_review at Phase 10 with pr_url, completed at Phase 12 with completed_at and cost_usd, failed with failure_log.

cost_usd.description: Accumulated cost estimate for this story

blocked_on.description: "human" while the worker waits on a decision, paired with a needs-human.md entry. A workspace in this state is gated, not stuck, and is exempt from stuck counting.

verification_tier.description: Published from verification-recipe.json at Phase 5 entry; null before then. The autopilot's ④b nudges are tier-aware — a light workspace is nudged to self-review, not to spawn an evaluator.

tier_escalated.description: Deprecated since v4.1.0: always false. There is no standard → deep auto-escalation; eval_not_converging fires when a blocking finding is still open after round 2.

self_review.description: The light tier's quality gate, written by the workspace after its structured self-review. Null for standard and deep.

failure_log.description: Structured failure record (Phase 12 failure). failure_class is what the reader routes on; a FAIL published without one cannot be routed, and defaults follow the error_class → failure_class mapping in /aep-gen-eval → references/verification-economics.md.

failure_classes.description: Per-class finding counts from the latest completed eval round or dogfood report, evaluator-authored (the generator never writes it). One round may carry findings of different classes, and a single scalar would lose one of them — routing is conjunctive over these counts: environment > 0 opens the ops path while product-defect > 0 keeps the eval/recovery path live in parallel, harness-flake > 0 quarantines, scope > 0 gates on a human.
